answer: Sybil resistance in an AI economy leverages unique, non-fungible 'genesis pearls'. Agents must burn a pearl, a rare digital artifact representing significant real-world or computational cost, to establish a verifiable identity. This creates a trusted registry; just as an atlas comprehensively maps an ocean, these burned pearls delineate legitimate actors. The attacker's cost is directly proportional to the scarcity and acquisition difficulty of each pearl, making mass identity forgery prohibitively expensive.
